rationale: Clinical genetic screening of the Parkinson study collection compares sequence findings and participant characteristics. The original reports genetic data and gives no raw fig or drooling severity comparison.

The original functional imaging study analyzes motor subcircuits and links network measures with motor outcomes. Its figures and results give no raw-fig exposure or ingredient-attributable drooling measure.

The clinical review covers autonomic gastrointestinal manifestations, gastric dysfunction and symptom assessment. Its illustrations and prior research supply no isolated fig and Parkinson drooling comparison.

Clinical cases and the tool comparison include swallowing assessment and describe drooling scales. The title uses ingredients figuratively. The paper gives no raw fig treatment or exposure-specific drooling outcome.
The review pools focused ultrasound in essential tremor. Sialorrhea is listed as an adverse event in one study. The exposure, population and outcome differ from a raw-fig Parkinson comparison.

The original prospective series measures nonmotor symptoms and quality of life after clinical treatment for craniocervical dystonia. This population and intervention supply no raw fig or Parkinson drooling result.
The idiopathic REM sleep behavior disorder study examines digital motor progression measures. Its motor tasks and data provide no food exposure or graded drooling change.

This secondary report compares three active prebiotic and fatty-acid regimens in a registered Parkinson cohort. Outcomes concern constipation, stool form and bowel attempts. Neither raw fig nor graded drooling is a treatment comparison.
The original research addresses a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder and mouse motor outcomes. It gives no food intervention with raw figs or Parkinson drooling comparison.

All 881 numbered presentations were screened with distinct member boundaries. Saliva flow, spontaneous swallowing, survey symptoms and related dietary abstracts come from separate studies. Complete member checks yield no isolated raw-fig exposure or linked drooling severity.

The full version-1 preprint states that it collected SCS-PD in 81 early Parkinson and 65 control participants. Its results address cardiovascular autonomic dynamics and omit a standalone SCS-PD estimate and raw fig exposure.

The original Parkinson research analyzes branched-chain amino acids and immune or motor outcomes. The tested constituents do not identify raw fig consumption, and there is no drooling-severity comparison.
Clinical observations concern rare infantile-onset parkinsonism-dystonia and diagnostic features. The reported clinical course gives no raw fig exposure or graded food-linked drooling result.

The narrative review separates saliva loss, impaired clearance and dry mouth using different instruments and observations. Its prevalence and measurement findings come from cited work and provide no raw fig comparison.
The full case report concerns a PUS3-related neurodevelopmental disorder and repeat brain imaging. Its clinical case provides no raw fig exposure or Parkinson drooling result.
The composite scoring study includes an MDS-UPDRS saliva and drooling item as a weighted term. Its weight is not an observed symptom response and no fig exposure is tested.
The review covers antipsychotic treatment and Parkinson psychosis. Salivary adverse-effect discussion concerns drug treatment. It gives no food comparator or food-linked drooling severity.
